scope: Frozen-v2 Chapters 1 and 2 titles, two fold titles and moved proof paragraphs, their connected explanations and reader-facing sidecar fields. No writer defenses read and no edits.
audience: Undergraduate calculus, basic probability and linear algebra; needed neural/stochastic meanings taught in the reading path.

heading_answers.passage: # Persistent neural activity can still accumulate memory error {#ch:FOUNDATIONS}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Removing the distinction between continued activity and accurate memory would lose the chapter question.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Persistent and error have ordinary meanings here; the opening immediately separates represented value from activities.

heading_answers.passage: ## Patterns of firing rates represent a value {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-SPIKES}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The rate-pattern statement gives the point of the coming cell-level definitions.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Firing rate is defined in the first paragraph; population code and decoding follow the explicit rate vector. A title preview does not require extra jargon before this explanation.

heading_answers.passage: ## A variable spike count at a fixed rate {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-POISSON}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Fixed rate with variable count is the needed observation that motivates the Poisson model.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Poisson process is the exact model name and is immediately given its count law, duration and expected count. Replacing it with random firing would erase the model assumptions.

heading_answers.passage: ## Mean squared displacement combines random spread with mean motion {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-COVARIANCE}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The title states why variance alone may not account for displacement; deleting mean motion would hide the later bias distinction.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Mean, variance and covariance belong to the audience probability baseline. The chapter gives subject-specific displacement and covariance meanings before using them for neural or eye signals.

heading_answers.passage: ## Stable activity with a vulnerable stored value {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-ATTRACTOR}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The short value-versus-activity contrast is the concrete reason for the attractor example.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Stable is explained as decay in a direction; vulnerable is ordinary wording for a value that can change. Continuous attractor and neutral direction receive exact definitions before the example depends on them.

heading_answers.passage: ## Independent steps with equal duration and variance give linear variance growth {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-DIFFUSION}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain the repaired title. Its duration and variance conditions earn their words because deleting either would broaden the mathematical claim.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Steps is ordinary language for the defined interval increments. Equal variance is appropriate for the probability baseline, and the body immediately identifies the shared 2D Delta t value.

heading_answers.passage: ## A fixed spatial map differs from a value that wanders over time {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-RANDOMNESS}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The contrast prevents using random spatial shape as evidence of temporal memory loss.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Fixed refers to the expected spatial function for a cell/environment, not invariant observed spikes; the first paragraph makes that meaning explicit.

heading_answers.passage: # Spiking noise produces diffusion along the memory attractor {#ch:MEMORY-DYNAMICS}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The title identifies the specific state direction in which spike noise accumulates.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Spiking and attractor are taught in Chapter 1. Diffusion has its variance-growth meaning there; the Chapter 2 notation paragraph recalls its convention before calculation.

heading_answers.passage: ## Recurrent spikes renew decaying synaptic activity {#sec:MEMORY-SPIKES}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Renew connects the decaying activation to the recurrent cause that can sustain it.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Recurrent means a circuit sends signals back into its population, defined in Chapter 1. The present first paragraph explains the full cycle rather than relying on that label.

heading_answers.passage: ## The network's return flow determines the lasting memory change {#sec:MEMORY-LINEARIZATION}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Return flow distinguishes the required projection from a perpendicular geometric shortcut; deleting it loses the section result.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Flow is used concretely as the state returning toward the fixed-point family. Linearization and both zero eigenvectors are defined with equations and purposes before the lasting-displacement result.

heading_answers.passage: ## Projecting spike fluctuations gives the diffusion coefficient {#sec:MEMORY-DIFFUSION}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The title names the calculation the reader can now perform from projected fluctuations.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Projecting has the specific left-vector meaning just taught. Diffusion coefficient is already defined and is now matched explicitly to increment variance.

heading_answers.passage: ## Symmetric weights express diffusion through tuning curves {#sec:MEMORY-SYMMETRIC}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The symmetry condition earns its place because it makes a tuning-based expression possible; removing it suggests the same formula works for all networks.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Symmetric weights are given as W_ij=W_ji in the opening. Tuning curves were introduced in Chapter 1, and their input/rate derivatives are defined before the formula.

heading_answers.passage: ## Long delay errors depend on boundaries and local diffusion {#sec:MEMORY-LONG-TIME}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Boundaries and state dependence explain why a local coefficient cannot alone fix all delay errors.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Local means evaluated near the current represented value, as stated in the preceding section. Probability density is from the probability baseline, and p is assigned its memory-trial meaning before the equation.

heading_answers.passage: ## A diffusion calculation does not determine systematic drift {#sec:MEMORY-DRIFT-SCOPE}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. The title preserves a needed limit on the preceding variance calculation.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Systematic drift is explained first as reproducible mean movement, then defined as nonzero mean velocity. Ito and Stratonovich retain their exact names because they describe different coefficient-evaluation rules.

heading_answers.passage: ## Figures distinguish memory motion from readout error and test diffusion {#sec:MEMORY-FIGURES}
heading_answers.deletion_test: Retain. Memory motion, readout uncertainty and simulation tests are different contributions; the heading helps the reader keep them apart.
heading_answers.terminology_answer: Readout error is explained in the figure paragraph as finite-spike uncertainty about current location. Activity bump is defined when first needed, and all empirical-versus-simulation labels remain precise.

fold_and_moved_passage_answers.title: Derivation: why a Poisson count has variance equal to its mean
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.deletion_test: Retain the exact calculation as optional depth. Deleting it would remove the count-variance derivation; leaving it visible is not required to understand the result already stated before it.
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.terminology: Poisson count and variance/mean are the exact concepts being derived. Factorial moments occurs inside the proof and is immediately shown as the sums of k and k(k-1), so no additional unexplained concept drives the result.
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.connected_text: The visible E[K]=Var(K)=lambda result comes first. After the fold, relative standard deviation and the silent-cell example use that visible result without referencing hidden proof notation.

fold_and_moved_passage_answers.title: Derivation: from random increments to the memory density equation
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.deletion_test: Retain the proof as optional depth because it connects local increments to density evolution. The visible first-pass solution and ring-limit discussion do not need its test-function algebra.
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.terminology: Random increments has its interval-change meaning from Chapter 1. Memory density here refers to p(theta,t), already defined for repeated trials in this section. Ito, Fokker Planck and Dirac delta are retained exact terms with local meanings supplied before later reasoning.
fold_and_moved_passage_answers.connected_text: The repaired first sentence states its purpose directly. The last sentence names the Fokker Planck equation explicitly. The later state-dependent-moment paragraph independently states its boundary condition and explains integration by parts; it does not rely on an unexplained object hidden in this fold.
